# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-09-01

# Section 1 — Executive Summary

The competitive set spans three tiers this week — hyper-local NoVA specialists (Mermaid), a national franchise (EcoWater), and a regional Tidewater/Richmond player (Hampton Roads) — but only **Mermaid is running aggressive, dollar-specific promotions** ($200 off heaters, $100 off first service, free installs), making them the pricing pace-setter to watch. The dominant industry playbook is uniform: lead with a **free water test as the conversion hook**, then upsell diagnosis-based treatment. Trust signals are the real battleground — Mermaid leans on 1,500+ 5-star reviews and Kinetico dealer status; Hampton Roads counters with a "Lifetime Warranty" and Made-in-USA claim. No competitor changed hero positioning or meta from last week's snapshot, so this is a **stable landscape where promotion aggressiveness, not messaging, is the current lever**.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table

| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Test first, install right, stand behind the work" (local water + plumbing) | Plumbing (heaters, drains, disposals), pump/pressure systems, commercial DI/RO, Kinetico dealer | Yes — $200 off heater, $100 off first service, free Kinetico install, free heater flush | No positioning/meta change; promo carousel is prominent |
| EcoWater | "Better Water Starts Here" (global leader, ~century of expertise) | Symptom-based diagnostic quiz, smart-home leak/conservation tech, 3rd-party certified systems, dealer network | No — "free water test" only | No change vs. prior snapshot |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Full-service water quality experts" (Tidewater + Richmond) | Water testing, hard water/bacteria/contaminant treatment, air treatment | No — "free water test," Lifetime Warranty (details on request) | No change vs. prior snapshot |
| *(5 competitors not provided in snapshot)* | — | — | — | Data missing — flag for next pull |

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave

- **Match or beat Mermaid's promo clarity.** They're the only one advertising hard dollar offers. Test a limited-time "new customer" incentive with a specific dollar figure — vague "free test" language is now table stakes, not a differentiator.
- **Own a warranty/certification claim explicitly.** Hampton Roads uses "Lifetime Warranty" and Made-in-USA; EcoWater uses third-party certification. ClearWave should surface its strongest trust proof (warranty terms, certifications, review count) above the fold to avoid looking generic.
- **Borrow the symptom-based entry funnel.** Both EcoWater ("if you experience… you may need…") and Mermaid ("start with the result you want") route visitors by problem, not product. Test a "What's wrong with your water?" selector as the primary CTA.

# Section 4 — Watch items

- **Only 3 of 8 competitor snapshots were provided** — request the remaining 5 for a complete read before next brief.
- **Mermaid's promo rotation** — confirm whether the $200/$100 offers are permanent or seasonal; if they expire, that's a window to out-promote them.

items.title: Water Minute · Why big-box water systems die at year 3
items.preview:
Words I like;
Buy nice or buy twice.
Here is what nobody tells you about that shiny water system from the big-box store.
The tank looks fine. The label looks fine. The problem is inside, where you cannot see it. Two things kill those units around year three.
First, the valve. The control valve is the brain of the whole system. It cycles every few days for years. Big-box units run a plastic-geared valve built to hit a price, not to last. Once those gears wear, the system stops regenerating, and your water quietly goes back to hard.
Second, the media. That is the actual working material inside the tank. Cheaper builds pack less of it, and lower grade, so it exhausts fast. Less media, more frequent failure. Simple math.
None of this shows up on the sticker. You find out when your soap stops lathering and your fixtures start crusting again.
If you own one of ours, this is exactly why your system is still humming along years in. You paid once for a valve and media built to go the distance, and it has been doing its job every single day since.

As promised, value in under a minute.
